newsitem.title: USA: US FCC to appeal court stay of phone rules.
newsitem.headline: US FCC to appeal court stay of phone rules.

text.p: The Federal Communications Commission said it will ask the U.S. Supreme Court to lift a partial stay of its landmark "interconnection" order issued earlier Tuesday by a U.S. appeals court in St. Louis.
"The Eighth Circuit stay throws a monkey wrench into the carefully designed congressional machinery for introducing competition into the local exchange market," said FCC Chairman Reed Hundt.
"We intend to go immediately to the Supreme Court. We will ask them to lift the stay, so that the congressional competition policy can promote investment and job growth all over the country."

The federal appeals court "stayed," or suspended, the pricing and "pick-and-choose" elements of the FCC "interconnection" order aimed at opening the $100 billion local phone market to long-distance carriers, cable-television operators and others. The stay is in effect until the court rules on the challenge some time next year.
